ev.q: Weighted percentages (with 95% CIs) of ventilation improvement strategies among K–12 public schools, including by locale and school poverty level, were estimated.
City schools were less likely to report opening windows when safe to do so (53.9%) than were suburban (69.5%)
Weighted percentages and 95% CIs are presented for each category.
Chi-square tests were used to test for differences in the percentage of schools reporting each ventilation strategy by school-level characteristics
City schools differed significantly from rural schools based on chi-square test (p<0.05).
A web-based survey is administered to school administrators (e.g., principals) or school-level designees
